title: Nasal swab for Staphylococcus aureus
what: This is a swab from your nose. It looks for Staphylococcus aureus, a common germ, and checks which medicines work against it.
why: Before planned surgery, for health workers, for frequent pimples and boils, or when infection control requires it.
duration: the swab takes less than a minute; results usually come in 3 to 5 days
tell_doctor: If you took antibiotics in the past few weeks
If you use nose ointments or drops
If you have planned surgery soon

prepare.title: Nose
prepare.text: For a few hours before the swab, do not rinse your nose or use drops or ointments, unless the doctor said otherwise.

prepare.title: Antibiotics
prepare.text: It is better to do the test before starting antibiotics. If you already take them, do not stop on your own. Tell your doctor.

prepare.title: Morning
prepare.text: The swab is usually taken in the morning. You can have breakfast, but do not gargle. Check with the lab.

steps: You sit down and tilt your head back a little
The nurse puts a swab a short way into one nostril
The swab is turned along the inside of the nose
The same is done in the other nostril
The swab is put in a tube
feel: It tickles, and you may want to sneeze
Sometimes your eyes water. It passes right away
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
If staph is found and you have no symptoms, treatment is not always needed. Your doctor decides
Do not start antibiotic ointments on your own

faq.q: Is staph in the nose an illness?
faq.a: Often not. Many healthy people carry it in the nose with no harm. Treatment is needed only in some cases.

faq.q: Why is this test done before surgery?
faq.a: To lower the risk of a wound infection. If the germ is found, the doctor may prescribe a treatment to clear it.

reminders.text: Nasal swab today. Until then, do not rinse your nose or use nose drops.
